newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures slink into long weekend.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures slink into long weekend.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Friday as players squared their positions ahead of a long weekend in Japan and the possibility of a U.S. rate hike.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract ended near the lower end of its 230-point range at 21,150 against a previous settlement at 21,320. Volume was a skimpy 11,712 lots.
Dealers said players were reluctant to maintain open positions with Japan closed for a holiday on Monday and the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting to determine monetary policy on Tuesday.
Market players are divided on the likelihood of an interest rate hike following a mixed bag of economic data and recent comments by Fed officials.

A trader with a Japanese institution said the market showed signs of heading lower to cover a gap that was created near the 20,940 level when the Nikkei opened sharply higher after a long weekend in Japan earlier in the week.
He said the December Nikkei could also come under some pressure from foreigners taking profits in the cash market.
